standard_prerequisites.name: Real integral Hodge conjecture and topological subgroup

statement.relation: Explicit BW1 prerequisite of the fixed PartII article; background only, no alias asserted to the published Inventiones version
statement.definition_summary: Let G=Gal(C/R). The restriction of alpha in H_G^{2k}(X(C),Z(k)) to X(R), followed by the canonical map(1.57), has components alpha_p for p congruent to k modulo2. The topological subgroup0 is defined by alpha_{k+i}=Sq^i(alpha_k) for even i, with negative squares zero. For1-cycles on a D-dimensional variety, k=D-1 and Remark1.20(i) equivalently requires alpha_p=0 for p<k. Over real numbers, Hdg_G0 intersects this subgroup with the inverse image of ordinary Hodge(k,k) classes. RIHC means surjectivity of CH^k(X) to Hdg_G0. PartII keeps its stated scope R=real numbers or H^2(O_X)=0.
statement.source_license_observation: The arXiv version declares its non-exclusive archive license; the PartII CC-BY4 license is not assigned to PartI. No PartI original TeX/PDF, proof or copied prose is redistributed here; this is a short mathematical paraphrase with a precise citation.

standard_prerequisites.role: Explicit definition background, editorial mathematical paraphrase only; no PartI raw proof/TeX/PDF copied or assigned PartII license.

standard_prerequisites.name: Real equivariant Hodge and curve-genus inputs from PartI
standard_prerequisites.statement: The author cites real Lefschetz(1,1), weak-Lefschetz Gysin surjectivity and the equivalence between the relevant real integral Hodge statement on rationally connected threefolds and the existence of a geometrically irreducible curve of even geometric genus. These remain explicit cited inputs. The local real infinitesimal criterion and actual Fano arguments are fully supplied.

standard_prerequisites.name: Infinitesimal variation and monodromy
standard_prerequisites.statement: Kodaira-Spencer, Griffiths variation, Green/Voisin infinitesimal density, Ehresmann and irreducibility of vanishing-cohomology monodromy are the author stated inputs. The equivariant adaptation, real fixed-locus restriction, integral-lattice/torsion recovery and real-to-complex parallel-transport argument are retained in full.

standard_prerequisites.name: Complex Fano anticanonical classification
standard_prerequisites.statement: Iskovskikh-Prokhorov Theorem2.1.16 and Proposition2.4.1 provide the three anticanonical branches and six double-cover cases. The actual author statement1670-1678 and all six uses1690-1756, including unique-base-point, even-genus intersections, delPezzo ramification and canonical nef-cone descent, are supplied. This known classification input is not re-proved or counted as a new PartII author question.

core_obligations: Include both the very-ample and not-very-ample branches, not only the infinitesimal criterion
Keep the fixed-locus real Hodge, torsion and integral-lattice details; complex rational Hodge reasoning alone is insufficient
Retain the complete author parallel-transport lemma and the real geometric descent cases
Do not assert arbitrary-real-closed extension, a uniform curve degree bound, existence of a conic, or applicability when the real locus is nonempty
proof_roadmap: Adapt the infinitesimal Noether-Lefschetz criterion to real Galois-invariant integral cycle classes.
For a very ample anticanonical K3 section, use vanishing cohomology and monodromy to produce the infinitesimal direction.
Use the empty-real-locus trace computation and Picard-rank bound to obtain a nonzero anti-invariant vanishing(1,1) class.
Treat the remaining anticanonical base-locus/double-cover classification cases by explicit real curves, ramification surfaces and descent of canonical contractions.
Apply the author cited even-genus/real-IHC equivalence in the remaining cases; do not split the branches into extra IDs.
items.difficulty_reason: H3: this is an integral real Hodge result whose author proof combines an equivariant Noether-Lefschetz deformation argument, real fixed-locus submersion and integral-lattice/torsion recovery, K3 vanishing cohomology and irreducible monodromy, and separate real descent arguments for the non-very-ample classification cases. The full local core and both proof branches are supplied; the complex classification and PartI equivalences remain identified cited inputs. Support propositions are not counted separately.
